summary: 🚀 LUNA-SAFE Project SummaryProject Name: LUNA-SAFE — Lunar Landing Intelligence & Site Evaluation SystemParticipant: Swanand Dindore (Solo Participant)   Core Problem: Lunar south pole exploration suffers from extreme lighting and communication constraints where low solar elevation causes power blackouts due to crater shadows, and Earth dips below the horizon, severing direct-to-Earth communication links.Our Solution: A high-performance mission control web application that evaluates landing sites by processing real solar and Earth ephemeris data relative to custom lunar coordinates.Key Features:Mission Dashboard: Clean, scientific dark-themed control center displaying real-time sun/earth elevations and visibility status.Solar & Earth Trackers: Interactive visualization charts tracking visibility windows.Suitability Scoring Engine: Algorithmic ranking of candidate locations (e.g., Shackleton Crater at Lat -89.9°, Lon 0.0°) based on concurrent power and communication availability.NASA Data Integration:NASA JPL Horizons System: Extracted precise ephemeris observer tables for the Sun (10) and Earth (399) relative to the lunar south pole.NASA LRO LOLA: Integrated digital elevation model references for surface topography and horizon analysis.Technology Stack: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and Lucide React.
details:
• What it does & How it works:
    LUNA-SAFE (Lunar Landing Intelligence & Site Evaluation System) is an advanced mission control web application designed to evaluate candidate lunar south pole landing sites (such as Shackleton Crater). It processes precise ephemeris observer tables and digital elevation models to track critical geometric parameters relative to custom lunar coordinates. Specifically, it computes solar elevation angles to determine photovoltaic power availability and tracks Earth's elevation relative to the local horizon to analyze direct-to-Earth radio line-of-sight status.
    • Frontend & Framework: JavaScript, React, Vite.
    • Styling & UI Components: Tailwind CSS, Lucide React icons.
    • Data Visualization: Recharts for dynamic solar and Earth elevation visibility curves.
    • Data Sources: NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris datasets and NASA LRO LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) digital elevation references.
  • Creativity & Design Factors Considered:
    LUNA-SAFE approaches lunar mission planning through a specialized, user-centric dark-themed mission-control aesthetic optimized for high-stress operational environments. Rather than relying on heavy, resource-intensive 3D engines that lag or fail on standard hardware, our design prioritizes lightweight, responsive data visualization, instant cross-platform accessibility, and transparent algorithmic scoring. Factors carefully evaluated during development include horizon obstruction limits, concurrent power-communication visibility windows, and strict adherence to verifiable ephemeris data without artificial simulation fabrication.
